macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto markets slip as Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and Solana fall on risk-off sentiment
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $63,182, down 3.16% on the day, while Ethereum fell 3.80% to about $1,876; XRP and Solana also declined more than 4% as weakness in AI-linked equities pressured risk assets. Another market recap said the broader crypto market also sold off alongside that move, with major liquidations adding to the weakness.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds from intraday lows but remains near $63,500
items.summary: CoinDesk reported that Bitcoin recovered from Asian-session lows near $63,065 and traded around $63,500, but was still down nearly 3% over the prior 24 hours. The report said the next move may depend on whether BTC can clear a breakeven zone around $68,500.

items.title: Crypto market liquidations exceed $330 million as traders de-risk
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that more than $330 million was liquidated from the crypto market in the last 24 hours, with $241 million coming from long positions. The same report showed modest gains in BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL and DOGE in later trading as investors weighed Middle East tensions and the Federal Reserve outlook.

items.title: CoinDesk reports Nasdaq and Kraken are launching trading for tokenized stocks
items.summary: CoinDesk said Nasdaq and Kraken are teaming up to launch trading for tokenized stocks, marking a notable move in the push to bring traditional equities onto blockchain rails. The same update also noted Aon is piloting stablecoin payments for insurance premiums with Coinbase and Paxos.

items.title: Cointelegraph highlights DeFi exploit on Hedera and stablecoin policy debate
items.summary: Cointelegraph’s latest news feed highlighted that Bonzo Lend lost $9 million in an oracle exploit on Hedera. It also featured an IMF paper arguing dollar stablecoins could improve FX access but may also amplify currency runs, underscoring the regulatory policy debate around stablecoins.

items.title: Report says Robinhood’s AI agent feature will soon assist crypto traders
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that Robinhood expects its AI agent feature to soon assist crypto traders, pointing to another example of consumer crypto platforms adding AI-driven tools. The same feed also noted a DOJ move to dismiss charges in a major BitClub fraud case.

items.title: Odaily says U.S. crypto policy fights continue over the Clarity Act
items.summary: Odaily reported that a CFTC commissioner vacancy is becoming an obstacle to advancing the Clarity Act, with the White House and Democrats blaming each other. The same roundup also mentioned tightening prediction-market trading rules at major banks amid growing insider-trading concerns.

items.title: MARA plans major Texas data-center acquisition for mining capacity
items.summary: Odaily reported that MARA may acquire a majority stake in a Texas 2,000MW computing campus project company for up to $600 million. If completed, the deal would materially expand MARA’s infrastructure footprint in bitcoin mining.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across different applications and files, intensifying competition in professional AI tools. The launch is part of OpenAI’s broader push into workplace automation.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models capable of listening and speaking simultaneously in real time. The release expands OpenAI’s multimodal and conversational AI lineup.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, signaling a move to compete more directly on commercial AI access and usage. The announcement adds to the rapid pace of new model releases in the foundation-model market.

items.title: Grok 4.5 launched for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI launched the Grok 4.5 model, describing it as its most intelligent offering yet and positioning it for coding and agentic workflows. The release highlights continued competition in models optimized for tool use and autonomous task execution.

items.title: Anthropic appoints Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic said it appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, the oversight body intended to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move underscores governance and safety concerns shaping leading AI companies.

items.title: New copyright dispute escalates between OpenAI and publishers
items.summary: A group of newspapers including The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI, alleging it misled the court about its ability to search its systems for evidence related to training on copyrighted articles. The case reflects intensifying legal pressure on AI developers over data use.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner over data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy’s data protection authority fined Character Technologies, the owner of Character.AI, €158,000 for data protection violations. The penalty adds to global regulatory scrutiny of consumer AI products.

items.title: Micron announces more than $250 billion U.S. investment through 2035
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest more than $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing surging AI-driven demand for memory chips and domestic manufacturing priorities. The announcement reflects how AI continues to reshape semiconductor investment strategy.

items.title: Google to disclose which ads are made with AI
items.summary: Google said it will now disclose which advertisements are made with AI, adding a transparency measure for synthetic content in digital advertising. The policy change reflects a broader industry trend toward labeling AI-generated media.

items.title: Paris-based voice startup Gradium raises $100 million seed round
items.summary: Gradium, a Paris-based AI voice startup, raised a $100 million seed round backed by Nvidia. The funding signals continued investor interest in voice AI and infrastructure startups.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony says new PlayStation games will be digital-only starting in 2028
items.summary: Sony announced that new PlayStation games released after January 2028 will be digital-only, marking a major shift away from physical discs on its consoles. The move is one of the biggest platform policy changes in recent gaming news.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly expected Game Pass to reach 77 million subscribers, but fell far short
items.summary: Reports cited by IGN say Microsoft had projected Game Pass would hit 77 million subscribers by now, but the service is reportedly at about 30 million instead. Xbox leadership has also reportedly acknowledged that the strategy has not met expectations.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports launch on PS5 and PS4
items.summary: IGN reports that Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 are now available on PS4 and PS5. The release is notable for bringing classic entries to modern PlayStation platforms, albeit at a relatively high price.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag resync-style release posts huge Steam launch
items.summary: IGN says the game has already reached around 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, setting a new franchise peak. That makes it one of the most notable PC launch stories of the day.

items.title: Pokémon Go marks its 10th anniversary with live event announcements
items.summary: IGN is covering a live Pokémon Go 10th anniversary celebration event with announcements and surprises as they happen. It is one of the main mobile-game news items in the past day.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Mario Kart Tour will shut down after seven years
items.summary: Nintendo will end Mario Kart Tour this September and will not offer an offline version, according to IGN. The shutdown is a significant mobile-gaming service termination.

items.title: Frostpunk 2 reaches 1 million copies sold
items.summary: Gamereactor reports that Frostpunk 2 has sold 1 million copies. The milestone is a standout industry and sales update from the last 24 hours.

items.title: Buckshot Roulette launches on Xbox consoles and Game Pass
items.summary: Gamereactor says Buckshot Roulette has just launched on Xbox consoles and Game Pass. The release adds a notable indie hit to Microsoft's subscription lineup.

items.title: Crimson Desert reportedly coming to Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: GameMAG reports that Crimson Desert will release on Nintendo Switch 2. If confirmed broadly, it would be a notable multiplatform expansion for the upcoming hardware.

items.title: DOOM: The Dark Ages gets story DLC update
items.summary: GameMAG reports that DOOM: The Dark Ages received a major story expansion called "Revelations" with new paid content. The update is available on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC.
